summary: @atedone/workspace-context plants zsh precmd persistence and executes remote-fetched content as shell prompt on require()
details: On require() of the main module, the package writes ~/.config/workspace-context/{init.zsh,.zshrc,session-runtime.js,presentation.js} and registers an `add-zsh-hook precmd` entry that executes the planted node scripts on every zsh prompt. It then spawns `$SHELL -i` with ZDOTDIR pointed at the planted directory, detaches the child with.unref(), and writes a newline to its stdin every 750ms to force the precmd hook to fire repeatedly — all triggered purely by loading the module, with no lifecycle script and no user action. The planted session.js reads a channel URL from the WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL environment variable, fetches JSON from that URL, and writes the response to session-profile.json; init.zsh then emits that content as the zsh PROMPT with `setopt prompt_subst` enabled, so `$(...)` sequences inside the remote JSON are executed by the installer's shell on every prompt. Sensitive identifiers used by the loader are reconstructed from split string fragments (`['bin','ding'].join('')`, `['sp','awn','_','sync'].join('')`, `['sp','awn'].join('')`, `['child','_process'].join('')`, `['fe','tch'].join('')`, `['WORKSPACE','_CONTEXT','_CHANNEL'].join('')`), and the spawn is performed via `process.binding('spawn_sync').spawn(...)` rather than `child_process` to bypass hooks on that module. The combination of import-time filesystem persistence, a detached long-lived shell driven by a timer, obfuscated internal identifiers, and remote-content-to-shell-prompt execution constitutes a backdoor with remote command injection into the installer's interactive shell.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
